evidence.claim: Constellation announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to support the launch of the Crane Clean Energy Center and restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1; Microsoft will purchase energy from the renewed plant as part of its goal to match PJM data-center power use with carbon-free energy.
evidence.source_title: Constellation to Launch Crane Clean Energy Center, Restoring Jobs and Carbon-free Power to the Grid

evidence.claim: Constellation reported Q1 2026 results and stated that its fleet had 55 GW of capacity across nuclear, natural gas, oil, geothermal, hydro, wind, and solar facilities, while emphasizing around-the-clock reliability for growing power demand.

CEG is best used in this funnel as a reference leader for nuclear-backed data-center power demand rather than an underfollowed chokepoint candidate, because it is a high-attention large-cap generator with direct hyperscaler contract evidence.
evidence.source_title: Constellation to Launch Crane Clean Energy Center, Restoring Jobs and Carbon-free Power to the Grid

evidence.claim: PPL's Q4 2025 investor update stated that Pennsylvania data-center requests in advanced stages increased to 25.2 GW and that signed agreements include customer protections such as prepayments, credit support, and minimum load demand.

evidence.source_title: PPL Corporation delivers solid first-quarter 2026 earnings; reaffirms full-year guidance and long-term growth targets

evidence.claim: PPL Electric Utilities announced that the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission approved a distribution-rate settlement including a new rate class with binding long-term financial and usage commitments for large users such as data centers.
evidence.source_title: Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission approves new distribution rates for PPL Electric Utilities prioritizing reliability, customer protections and long-term affordability

memory_update.text: CEG maps to nuclear_power_generation and data_center_power_demand as a reference leader with direct Microsoft/Crane Clean Energy Center PPA evidence; use it as a benchmark for nuclear-backed data-center power demand, not as an underfollowed discovery candidate.

PPL maps to regulated_grid_capex, large_load_interconnection_policy, and data-center-driven load growth; its Pennsylvania data-center pipeline and approved large-load rate class make it a useful utility-side validation ticker.

HON maps to the nuclear_fuel_cycle conversion_bottleneck through Honeywell Metropolis Works/ConverDyn, but public-equity purity is low because the exposure is embedded in a mega-cap diversified industrial.

For CEG, verify incremental economics from data-center PPAs, nuclear restart timing, NRC/regulatory approvals, fleet availability, and capacity-market effects before treating demand growth as fully monetized.
For PPL, verify conversion of data-center pipeline requests into signed agreements, connected load, reimbursable upgrades, allowed returns, and actual rate-base growth.

For HON, verify whether uranium conversion revenue, capacity utilization, DOE awards, or ConverDyn economics are material enough to matter for Honeywell shareholders; otherwise keep HON as node context only.

This candidate chunk contains no underfollowed small/mid-cap candidate; later Layer 2B chunks should prioritize purer suppliers one or two steps away from the obvious demand drivers, including grid hardware, transformers, switchgear, electrical services, and nuclear-fuel-cycle specialists.

summary: Mapped the candidate chunk as a reference-only relationship set for Energy. CEG anchors the nuclear-backed 24/7 clean-power demand lane tied to data-center procurement; PPL anchors the regulated-utility grid-capex and large-load interconnection lane; HON preserves the uranium-conversion bottleneck node but has low public-equity purity because Metropolis Works/ConverDyn is embedded inside a mega-cap diversified industrial. No underfollowed alpha candidate is present in this chunk; these tickers should mainly serve as benchmark/context names for comparing purer small/mid-cap grid, transformer, switchgear, fuel-cycle, or services suppliers in later layers.
